quotes.text:
/**
   * Notification that properties of a message have changed. Currently limited to
   * "keywords" and "junkscore". Only user-initiated changes for "junkscore" are
   * reported (filters via `nsMsgDBFolder::SetJunkScoreForMessages` and UI via
   * `nsMsgDBView::ApplyCommandToIndices`).
   *
   * @param aMsg The message header of the changed message.
   * @param aProperty The changed property.
   * @param aOldValue The value before the change.
   * @param aNewValue The value after the change.
   */
  void msgPropertyChanged(in nsIMsgDBHdr aMsg, in string aProperty,
                          in AUTF8String aOldValue, in AUTF8String aNewValue);

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The native msgPropertyChanged interface is documented for keywords and junkscore, with old/new UTF-8 string values. Folder keyword mutations notify only when a keyword was actually added or removed. Junk mutations capture the old score before writing the new score. Do not assume every arbitrary database-property write emits this notification. Keep native string values separate from the extension property bags derived from them. Static source and test inspection only. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check ran. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion is pending.
title: Message property notifications carry old and new string values at the native boundary
